articles.title: ‘Absolutely ridiculous’: Marizanne Kapp slams Cricket Australia’s decision on Anaya Bangar
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp has strongly criticised Cricket Australia’s decision to offer transgender cricketer Anaya Bangar a .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp has strongly criticised Cricket Australia’s decision to offer transgender cricketer Anaya Bangar a pathway back into competitive women’s cricket, calling the development “absolutely ridiculous” and saying it “should not be allowed”.Kapp’s reaction came after Australian media reported that Cricket Australia (CA) had cleared Anaya, the daughter of former India cricketer and coach Sanjay Bangar, to return to competitive cricket under its Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. The decision has since become a major talking point in the cricketing world.Sharing a report on her Instagram, Kapp wrote: “Absolutely ridiculous. This should not be allowed.”Anaya underwent gender-affirming surgery in March this year and has now been given a pathway towards elite women’s cricket in Australia. Under CA’s decision, she can play community cricket in any state or territory of Australia until March 2027.CA clears pathway for Anaya to return to competitive cricketFrom March 2027, Anaya can become eligible for elite-level women’s cricket if she continues to meet the policy requirements, including the stipulated testosterone threshold.An expert panel comprising CA’s Head of Integrity Jacqui Partridge, Integrity Partner and Legal representative Emily Yates, Head of Scheduling, Operations and Domestic Cricket Peter Roach, Anti-Doping Medical Officer Dr Peter Harcourt and Team Doctor Dr Pip Inge considered Anaya’s case before confirming the pathway.“Under Cricket Australia's Policy, a player seeking to participate in the female category of Elite Cricket must establish that their serum testosterone concentration has been below 10 nmol/L continuously for a period of no less than 12 months,” CA said in an email to Anaya.The governing body added that, based on the medical information submitted, the requirement would be satisfied in March 2027. Her eligibility from that point will remain conditional on a blood test confirming that her testosterone level remains below 10 nmol/L and that she continues to meet the policy’s requirements.Anaya said the process was neither “automatic or informal” and that CA had considered her medical and surgical history, hormone and testosterone levels, cricketing background, playing footage and scientific and athletic performance work conducted with Manchester Metropolitan University’s Institute of Sport.She also revealed that her most recent blood test in July recorded total testosterone at 0.6 nanomoles, which she said was within the female reference range reported by the laboratory.Anaya: ‘Eligibility is not selection’For Anaya, however, the CA decision represents an opportunity rather than a guarantee of a place in elite cricket.“I want to make another point very clearly. Eligibility is not selection. Cricket Australia has given me a pathway, which does not mean that I have been given a place in a team. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,” she said.“I don't expect my history or my identity to earn me a place on a cricket team. I want my cricket to earn me a place on a cricket team,” she added.Anaya acknowledged the high standard of women’s cricket and the legitimate debate surrounding fairness and competitive integrity in women’s sport, but argued that inclusion and fairness need not be mutually exclusive.“This is why I respect the process Cricket Australia has followed in considering my case,” she said, adding that one of the most difficult possibilities she had faced after transitioning was that cricket might no longer have a place for her.She said she had spent years trying to find a way back and that CA’s decision had finally given her “a pathway to try”.Anaya’s pathway could eventually include an opportunity to pursue the Women’s Big Bash League, provided she meets the eligibility requirements in March 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jofra Archer: England's 'box-office' fast bowler touches 94 mph in blistering spell against Pakistan at Lord's
articles.summary: Mark Wood hails "high quality" England bowling performance as they dismiss Pakistan for 110 on day two of second Test at Lord's; Jofra Archer averages 90.7 mph in fastest opening spell of his Test career; Ollie Robinson is taking wickets at 8.84 a piece this summer
articles.body:
England skittled the visitors for 110 in their first innings , with Ollie Robinson taking 4-11, Archer 3-26 and Josh Tongue 2-27, with Archer having set the tone with a blistering five-over burst before lunch that brought the opening breakthrough.

According to CricViz , Archer's opening spell averaged 90.7 mph, with the odd delivery touching 94 mph. He picked up the flat-footed Shan Masood caught behind as Pakistan limped to lunch at 16-2 after 14.1 overs of superb pace bowling.

"That was quality, high quality," England fast bowler Mark Wood enthused on Sky Sports Cricket . "If you want to come and watch international sport at its very best, this was it.

"England were relentless with their line and length and passed it on to the next bowler and the next. It was top quality.

"Pakistan didn't do a lot wrong but the scoreboard didn't go anywhere because they were under pressure.

"Archer was very fast and intimidating, he ran in hard and just kept getting quicker and quicker.

"You could almost feel how uncomfortable it was for the batters from the commentary box."

Sky Sports Cricket 's Nasser Hussain pointed to England's varied attack as adding an extra layer of difficulty for Pakistan.

Tongue struck twice either side of the lunch interval, with Abdullah Shafique (5) and Babar Azam (8) poking edges through to the wicketkeeper and third slip, respectively, while Robinson overturned a couple of 'not out' lbw decisions on field on his way to stunning figures of 4-11 from 13 overs.

He is now averaging a staggering 8.84 with the ball since his return to the Test team earlier this summer.

"The challenge of facing this England bowling attack is the difference in paces, skills and angles," Hussain said.

"Robinson has a very high release point and is bang on the perpendicular, which allows him to get bounce.

"Tongue is so far past the perpendicular, so that's why he finds angles to open the right-handers up and make them vulnerable to nicking off.

"And it was a box-office opening spell from Archer."

Broad: No luck for Archer | Pacer jokes he could 'play until 40'

Archer continued to prove a pest to Pakistan throughout the day, albeit without benefiting from a great deal of luck as he repeatedly threatened both edges of the bat - Azan Awais (46) playing and missing as many as 14 times to the quick.

He'd ultimately helped clean up the tail - Pakistan's final five wickets falling for just 19 runs - to finish with 3-26.

"He had no luck," former England seamer Stuart Broad said on Sky Sports Cricket . "He could have been walking away with a five-for today, Archer.

"The pace, the skill, he swung and seamed the ball, while he also bowled a couple of beautiful bouncers.

"England have been brilliant with the ball. We know this pitch is moving, but you've still got to get the ball in the right areas and threaten, and England, to a man, were on the money.

"They were relentless, they gave no free, cheap boundaries away. It looked a really impressive bowling unit."

Archer, meanwhile, believes a lack of luck has been a recurring theme for him of late.

"I haven't had luck for a few weeks now but when you are bowling you have to hang in there because when wickets come, they come in buckets," he told Sky Sports Cricket .

"With Azan today, I have never seen someone play and miss so many balls and not get out, so whatever he did, fair play to him."

Archer, feeling fresh, added: "It is nice having extra seamers in the line-up. Everybody is fit and firing and every day it will be someone else's turn.

"I bowled 12 overs today; in the last game I bowled nine, so it's unbelievable.

"I can probably play until 40 at this rate!"

Watch day three of England's second Test match against Pakistan at Lord's live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10.15pm on Saturday. Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream no contract

articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Archer, Robinson, Tongue and Atkinson impress and 'could trouble Australia'
articles.summary: Former England captain Michael Vaughan predicts England's new pace quartet will trouble Australia - so what is making them effective against Pakistan?
articles.body:
Any praise for England's pace attack this summer comes with the caveat of the quality of Pakistan's batting - and the fact they are operating in helpful home conditions.

But, after having their hand forced by the retirement of Ben Stokes, England have stumbled on something encouraging.

A four-man pace attack of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson, who dismissed Pakistan for 110 on day two of the second Test at Lord's , appears potent and, perhaps crucially for the future, are complementing each other in different ways...

Sarfaraz denies knowing about Pakistan threat to end tour

After the first-Test win at Headingley, captain Joe Root said his pace bowlers "do not know how good they can be" and praised the variety they offer.

Root suggested this group is ahead of bowling stocks from his previous stint as captain, when he often called upon right-arm seamers James Anderson, Stuart Broad, Chris Woakes and Ben Stokes, in terms of their variation.

The most obvious differential between his new quartet is pace - something brought into further focus by England's decision to prioritise bowlers who reach high speeds during last winter's Ashes defeat.

While Archer was touching 95mph in the quickest opening spell of his career on day two at Lord's, Robinson was operating around 78mph at the other end.

Tongue's average pace across the series is actually higher than Archer, though Archer has bowled a higher percentage of his deliveries over 90mph.

Atkinson slots in just below Tongue and Archer, who joked he could play until he is 40 given how his team-mates are sharing the load.

"It is a good attack," said former England captain Michael Vaughan. "They can all get better and that is a really good sign.

"This batting line-up is possibly the easiest I have seen to bowl to but this attack, bowling the way they are doing, will challenge better batting line-ups.

"They will challenge the Australia line-up quite nicely if they bowl like this."

What Robinson has lacked in pace, he is making up for with skill. Four more wickets on Friday took him to 17 wickets at an average of 8.84 across his three Tests this summer.

Helped by lively English pitches, Robinson has been able to concentrate on his greatest skill - his control of line and length.

Against Pakistan, he has hit a good length with 70% of his deliveries. Atkinson has the next best record with 52%.

It has meant Robinson has been relentlessly testing the defences of Pakistan's batters, while giving them few bad balls to hit.

He bowled 31 deliveries in a row without conceding a run on Friday and 13 overs, which cost only 11 runs, were the most economical figures by a pace bowler bowling 10 overs or more in England for 13 years.

"Ollie Robinson is an extraordinarily skillful bowler," said Vaughan.

"[England] are trying to get him to 81mph more consistently and if he can get to that he will challenge all batting line-ups in all conditions.

"He has been the tone-setter we were crying out for in the winter."

England's 2005 pace attack of Stephen Harmison, Andrew Flintoff, Matthew Hoggard and Simon Jones is their best in terms of its all-round threat.

Harmison and Flintoff provided pace and bounce, Jones the skiddier threat and Hoggard genuine swing.

While Robinson and Archer can operate as swing bowlers as well as bowling their more natural seam, this current group's variety comes more from their plans and their specific characteristics.

Archer and Robinson have particularly high release points, while Tongue delivers the ball from notably wide on the crease - 96.4cm from the stumps compared with Archer's 40.3cm - with his unusual, beyond-the-perpendicular action.

Atkinson, who took 34 wickets at 20.17 in his first year in Test cricket in 2024, is the all-rounder who bowls accurately, but does so at a higher pace than Robinson.

"You want a bowler who can swing it, another bowler who has proper pace, another who can reverse swing it and another who can do the donkey work," said BBC chief cricket commentator Jonathan Agnew.

"It is a well-balanced attack but without the spinner."

Archer's natural angle makes him particularly effective against left-handers.

He averages 23.9 against southpaws compared with 31.3 against right-handers - helpful for England because Tongue and Atkinson's records are almost a mirror image.

Tongue averages 21.5 against right-handers but 35.7 against lefties. Atkinson's record is 19.9 compared with 31.7.

Tongue's position on the crease also aids him in his speciality of targeting the stumps.

Across this series, 22% of Tongue's deliveries would have hit the timbers while a figure of 29% at Headingley, where he took eight wickets across the first Test, was the highest by an England bowler in a home Test for 15 years.

And after two more wickets on Friday, Tongue's bowling strike-rate now stands at a dismissal once every 39.8 balls, putting him 12th on the list of bowlers to have taken 30 Test wickets.

"Tongue is the one who is really developing the best of them," Agnew said.

A home Ashes series is less than one year away. England's bowlers appear to be shaping up nicely.

articles.title: Imran Khan: Sarfaraz Ahmed says Pakistan players did not know about boycott threat
articles.summary: Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed says he and his players did not know about a Pakistan Cricket Board threat to the England and Wales Cricket Board over a Sky interview with the sons of Imran Khan.
articles.body:
Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said he and his players did not know about a Pakistan Cricket Board threat to the England and Wales Cricket Board over a Sky interview with the sons of Imran Khan.

During lunch on day one of the second Test, Sky Sports aired an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran, who has been in prison for the past three years.

It is understood the PCB raised the prospect of cancelling the Test at Lord's and the remainder of the three-match tour if the interview aired.

A version of the interview was broadcast, and the players returned to the field after the interval to continue the match.

"I don't know anything. I'm just focusing on the match," said Sarfaraz at the end of the second day's play.

"You're talking about the interview? We don't know about the interview."

Asked if there was ever a possibility his players would return for the afternoon session on day one, the former Pakistan wicketkeeper said: "All are OK. We were having lunch at that time."

Legendary all-rounder Imran Khan, 73, had a 21-year international career for Pakistan and famously led his team to World Cup glory in 1992.

He served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022. Since 2023, Khan has been in jail on corruption charges which he denies.

Ex-cricket captains urge 'proper medical care' for Imran Khan

The PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi also serves as Pakistan's interior minister.

In the interview conducted by former England captain Michael Atherton, Suleiman and Kasim expressed concerns over the treatment and security given to their father, as well as criticising the UK government's response.

Before it aired, Sky received a complaint about the plan to broadcast the interview.

In response to the tension around the situation, the ECB took government advice from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

In Pakistan, the match is being aired by the public broadcaster PTV, using Sky's pictures. PTV did not air the interview.

Ultimately, the tourists resumed play after lunch and the Test has continued to the end of the second day, with England 261 runs ahead at 81-3 in their second innings.

It is understood Sky received no further complaints on Friday in relation to the interview.

In October, England will tour Pakistan for a one-day tri-series against the home side and Sri Lanka.

It will be England's fourth separate tour of Pakistan in the past four years following a 17-year gap between visits to the country because of security concerns.

In 2006, a Test between England and Pakistan at The Oval was abandoned after the visitors were accused of ball tampering.

Pakistan were adjudged to have forfeited the match after refusing to play after tea on the fourth day, the only instance in Test history when a team has forfeited a Test.

We don't know about the interview," Sarfaraz told reporters.The Pakistan coach was then asked whether there had been any possibility of the players refusing to return for the second session on the opening day."All are OK. They also questioned the UK government’s response to his situation.A version of the interview was ultimately broadcast, despite the reported concerns raised by the PCB.In Pakistan, however, viewers did not see the interview. articles.title: ‘India messed up big time’: Ex-captain sounds alarm after costly Colombo blunder
articles.summary: Cricket News: India’s World Test Championship hopes have taken a hit after the Colombo Test ended in a draw, with former India cricketer Krishnamachari Srikkanth wa.
articles.body: India’s World Test Championship hopes have taken a hit after the Colombo Test ended in a draw, with former India cricketer Krishnamachari Srikkanth warning that the missed opportunity could have serious consequences for their qualification campaign.India appeared well placed to complete a 2-0 series sweep after taking control of the second Test. Sri Lanka began the final day with six wickets down, leaving India needing only four more wickets to seal victory.Instead, the visitors could manage just two wickets as Sonal Dinusha produced a stunning unbeaten century to frustrate India. The Sri Lankan batter remained unbeaten on 133 and stitched together vital partnerships with the lower order, helping the hosts survive and force a draw after following on.The result meant India had to settle for a 1-0 series victory rather than the 2-0 sweep that had looked within reach.The dropped opportunity in Colombo could prove significant in the race for the WTC Final. India remain fifth in the standings, with Sri Lanka sixth, and now have very little room for error across their remaining seven Tests.According to Srikkanth, India may need an almost perfect run from here to stay in control of their qualification hopes."This draw will make it difficult for India to qualify for the WTC final. Even if India wins five or six of the last seven matches, they'll have to depend on other results. It's questionable if India can beat Australia 5-0 at home. If we give rank turners in that series, Australia can also beat India," Srikkanth said on his YouTube channel.India have seven Tests left in their WTC campaign and need to win at least six of them to control their own destiny.A major challenge will come when Australia travel to India. Srikkanth cautioned against assuming that home conditions will guarantee results, particularly if India prepare heavily turning pitches.Srikkanth was particularly critical of India’s failure to close out the Colombo Test after creating a strong position.He also highlighted Dinusha’s contribution, with the Sri Lankan batter producing twin centuries at the Sinhalese Sports Club and playing a decisive role in keeping his team alive on the final day."India messed up big time. Sonal Dinusha was amazing throughout the series. This is where you miss a bowler like Bumrah. You need a finishing bowler like him. Though rain helped Sri Lanka a bit, India should have won the match hands down," said Srikkanth.Dinusha’s unbeaten 133 proved crucial as Sri Lanka survived India’s late push and secured a draw, leaving the visitors with a 1-0 series win but also a potentially costly setback in their WTC campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'He keeps faking injuries': Former Pakistan chief selector's explosive allegation against Imam-ul-Haq
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan opener Imam-ul-Haq’s calf injury has come under fresh scrutiny after former chief selector Mohammad Wasim made a startling claim about the ba.
articles.body: Pakistan opener Imam-ul-Haq’s calf injury has come under fresh scrutiny after former chief selector Mohammad Wasim made a startling claim about the batter’s history of allegedly faking injuries.Imam was ruled out of the remainder of the Lord’s Test against England after suffering a left calf strain while fielding on the opening day. However, Wasim has now alleged that the batter had previously used injury concerns to avoid playing, and claimed he was warned about one such incident before it happened.Speaking about Imam’s alleged injury history, Wasim said:"In 2022 Multan test, the physio warned me in advance that he is going to fake an injury soon. And he did that."Wasim’s remarks have added another layer to the controversy surrounding Imam, who missed Pakistan’s ongoing second Test against England after the Pakistan Cricket Board confirmed that scans showed a low-grade calf strain.What happened at Lord’s?Imam picked up the injury during the opening day of the Lord’s Test and spent time away from the field during Thursday’s evening session.The PCB subsequently confirmed the nature of the injury."Scans later confirmed a low-grade calf strain and Imam is currently receiving treatment under the supervision of the Pakistan medical team," the PCB said."His participation in the remainder of the Test depends on treatment leading to recovery," it added.Imam had opened the innings alongside young Azan Awais during the first Test at Leeds, which Pakistan lost by an innings inside three days.He was subsequently unable to take part in the remainder of the Lord’s Test, leaving Pakistan without one of their established opening batters.Pakistan struggle continuesPakistan’s problems at Lord’s extended well beyond Imam’s absence.England took a commanding position after bowling Pakistan out for just 110, securing a first-innings advantage of 180 runs. The visitors had yet to reach 180 in an innings during the series.England’s pace attack made the most of the conditions, with Ollie Robinson producing figures of 4-11 from 13 overs, including six maidens. Jofra Archer claimed 3-26 from 11.2 overs, while Josh Tongue took two wickets and Gus Atkinson went wicketless.Pakistan were dismissed in only 37.2 overs, having returned to bat less than a few hours after England had been bowled out for 290.By the end of the second day, England had stretched their overall lead to 261 runs after reaching 81-3 in their second innings before bad light brought an early close.Khurram Shahzad and Mohammad Ali did manage to remove Ben Duckett, Jordan Cox and Joe Root in the final session, but England remained firmly in control.Wasim’s allegation now puts the spotlight on Imam’s injury record, although the PCB has officially diagnosed his latest setback as a low-grade calf strain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BCCI stance on Sports Bill creates confusion within Board
articles.summary: Cricket News: New Delhi: A recent development in a matter concerning the Odisha Cricket Association’s (OCA) elections in the Odisha High Court has created confusion.
articles.body: New Delhi: A recent development in a matter concerning the Odisha Cricket Association’s (OCA) elections in the Odisha High Court has created confusion among the Indian cricket board’s (BCCI) state units over the National Sports Governance Act, passed in 2025.In an affidavit filed by the BCCI’s legal team and authorised by board secretary Devajit Saikia, it has been claimed that the OCA must conduct its elections as per the existing BCCI constitution, which was amended following the Lodha Committee recommendations in 2019.The BCCI has asserted that cricket is not a ‘designated sport’ even though the Act has been enacted, suggesting its reluctance to come under the ambit of the National Sports Board (NSB).Several state associations were under the impression that fresh elections would remain in abeyance until December 2026, as per the sports ministry’s notice issued last December. The biggest point of friction is the cooling-off period for office-bearers. The Act does not specify any cooling-off period and also relaxes certain areas related to conflict of interest.The incumbent OCA office-bearers have claimed that they are following the government’s directions, while the BCCI has taken an opposite stance.“It is submitted that even though the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 has been enacted, the sport of cricket has not been notified as a ‘designated sport’ for the said National Sports Governance Act, 2025 to apply,” the BCCI’s affidavit stated.“That Odisha Cricket Association has similar provisions of no office-bearer continuing for more than two terms consecutively, it is imperative that timely elections should be held in order to avoid continuation of any person for more than two terms consecutively and to uphold the spirit of the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court,” the affidavit, a copy of which is with TOI, read.The next hearing is scheduled for September 1.Interestingly, during a parliamentary discussion in August 2025, Vijayawada MP and Andhra Cricket Association president Kesineni Sivanath welcomed the bill and stated that the BCCI already adheres to its core principles.It was mentioned that the government had only exempted the BCCI from coming under the ambit of the Right to Information (RTI) Act since it did not depend on public funds. In May, the Central Information Commission, while exempting the BCCI from the RTI Act, stated that the Lodha Committee’s recommendations were only ‘advisory in nature’.The BCCI’s recent stance has created an ambiguous situation within the board.“If the government has notified that sports bodies can defer elections till December 2026, every state unit would believe it can wait until then before holding elections for select posts. The power forces in BCCI have always advocated the importance of continuity in administration. The board’s reluctance to adhere to government directives can disrupt it just when the new office-bearers were gaining experience.“It has also created confusion over the governance of the sport. The state bodies need to know if they have to follow the Sports Governance Act or the BCCI constitution,” a senior official told TOI.The BCCI held its elections last September, before the sports ministry issued its advisory. BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla will complete six years in office next year, while secretary Saikia is into his second term as an office-bearer and will complete six years in 2028 before entering the cooling-off period under the BCCI constitution.If the BCCI eventually comes under the ambit of the NSB, the mandatory cooling-off period would not apply to its office-bearers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 90.7 mph average speed: Jofra Archer bowls fastest spell of Test career; calls speed guns 'dodgy'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Jofra Archer produced the fastest spell of his Test career as England bowled Pakistan out for 110 on Day 2 of the second Test at Lord’s and took compl.
articles.body: Jofra Archer produced the fastest spell of his Test career as England bowled Pakistan out for 110 on Day 2 of the second Test at Lord’s and took complete control of the match.England’s pace attack made full use of the conditions after Pakistan resumed with hopes of staying in the game. Ollie Robinson finished with 4/11, Archer took 3/26 and Josh Tongue returned 2/27 as Pakistan were dismissed for 110, giving England a first-innings lead of 180 runs.Archer set the tone with a five-over spell before lunch that brought the first breakthrough. According to CricViz, his opening spell averaged 90.7 mph, with some deliveries touching 94 mph. He dismissed Pakistan captain Shan Masood, who was caught behind, as the visitors went into lunch at 16/2 after 14.1 overs.Despite the numbers on the speed gun, Archer said he was not convinced they were accurate.“Nah, the speed gun isn’t working properly,” the 31-year-old said. “I saw some of them [speeds] and I was like, it didn’t really feel that way. I don’t know who’s up in the box working it, but thanks. I remember playing here in the Ashes in 2019 and thinking the same thing. Maybe the speed guns are a little bit dodgy here.”Robinson and Tongue continued the pressure after Archer’s opening burst. Archer praised the pace attack for working together rather than relying on one bowler.“Everyone chips in. Ollie’s been phenomenal since he started [playing] again. Gus and Tonguey, everyone’s picking up the slack,” Archer said. “With this attack you don’t have to go and do too much. You don’t have to try too hard. You know someone’s going to back you up.”Pakistan’s batting struggled throughout the innings. Opener Azan Awais was the only batter to offer resistance with 46, before pulling Robinson to deep square leg. Saud Shakeel was the next highest scorer with 16.England ended the day on 81/3 in their second innings, extending their overall lead to 261 runs.Even with rain forecast on Day 3, England remain in a commanding position as they look to secure their first home Test series win in two years.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘India took it for granted’: Ex-cricketer reveals how Virat Kohli could have changed Colombo result
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mohammad Kaif believes India missed the intensity and urgency needed to force a result in the Colombo Test, suggesting Virat Kohli’s presence could ha.
articles.body: Mohammad Kaif believes India missed the intensity and urgency needed to force a result in the Colombo Test, suggesting Virat Kohli’s presence could have made a difference on a frustrating final day.India were in a strong position to complete a 2-0 series sweep but could not finish the job after Sri Lanka resumed the final day with six wickets down. The visitors managed only two more dismissals, while Sonal Dinusha produced an unbeaten century to help the hosts secure a draw.The result left India with a 1-0 series victory and made their road to the World Test Championship Final considerably tougher. India remain fifth in the WTC standings, with Sri Lanka sixth, and now have little room for error with seven Tests remaining.India need to win at least six of those seven matches to keep control of their qualification hopes, with Australia also among their remaining opponents.Kaif questions India’s intensityKaif felt the Colombo setback was partly down to India failing to maintain the kind of energy required during a long Test match.The former India batter pointed towards Kohli’s leadership style, particularly the way the former captain would constantly communicate with his teammates and keep the intensity high even during extended periods in the field.“Playing Tests isn’t everyone’s cup of tea, boss. It’s a very long game and you have to keep bowling continuously. I felt that if someone like Virat Kohli had been playing this match, he would have been constantly shouting and keeping his team switched on," Kaif said.According to Kaif, India appeared to believe that Sri Lanka’s resistance would eventually collapse because of the assistance available to the spinners, rather than actively creating pressure to force wickets.“At times, I felt we took things for granted, thinking, ‘Just keep bowling, it will happen. The ball is turning so much, it will happen on its own," Kaif said.‘Result would have been different’Sri Lanka’s lower order and Dinusha’s resistance eventually frustrated India, with the batter remaining unbeaten on 133 and playing a crucial role in saving the Test.Kaif argued that India needed to manufacture pressure rather than wait for opportunities to arrive. He also felt the team lacked the energy that Kohli traditionally brought to the field.“We created very few things ourselves. Our energy levels were also very low. That is why I am saying, if Virat Kohli had been playing this Test, the result would have been different," Kaif said.He suggested Kohli would have constantly pushed his teammates to stay aggressive and would have directly challenged Dinusha during his marathon resistance.“The reason is that he would have been telling everyone, ‘Come on, Sarfaraz, come on, Jaiswal’ and he would have gone after Sonal as well. Who were we getting into confrontations with? We were getting into confrontations with Kumara," Kaif added.The draw means India now face a demanding stretch in their WTC campaign, where further dropped opportunities could significantly hurt their chances of finishing among the top two.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pat Cummins joins the rallying cry for Imran Khan
articles.summary: Off the field News: LONDON: The deteriorating health of imprisoned former Pakistan cricket captain Imran Khan continues to cause great alarm among the international crick.
articles.body: LONDON: The deteriorating health of imprisoned former Pakistan cricket captain Imran Khan continues to cause great alarm among the international cricketing fraternity. Expressing deep concern over his condition, cricketers demanded that he gets private medical treatment, is seen by his own doctors and is allowed family visits.On Friday, Pat Cummins became perhaps the first active cricketer to voice his support for Imran's medical care. "I hope Imran Khan is treated with the dignity anyone deserves," the Australia's Test and ODI captain posted on X."I hope the court ordered medical assessment be allowed to run its course, and that family visits continue," he said, quoting a short clip of former Australian cricketer Greg Chappell on his podcast."Adding my support here to GC (Greg Chappell) and the other former international captains. I hope the court ordered medical assessment to be allowed to run its course, and that family visits continue," Cummins' plea added.Speaking on the Grade Cricketer podcast, Chappell earlier said, "He has been in isolation for three years. I don't think he is allowed books to read. He is in the dark most of the time. Nobody should be kept in those conditions. "I know there has been a tradition in Pakistan to have former prime ministers land up in jail, but this is over and above."Whilst no Pakistan cricketers signed Sunday's letter, Javed Miandad, former Pakistan captain and Imran's former teammate, is reportedly trying to visit him in jail. Imran's plight found centrestage during the ongoing Lord's Test between England and Pakistan, when his sons Sulaiman and Kasim, gave an interview to former England captain Michael Atherton during lunch on Thursday. Broadcast by Sky Sports, it prompted a formal complaint from the Pakistan Cricket Board. In Pakistan, PTV, which is broadcasting the series, did not show the 18-minute interview.Kasim told Atherton, "It's very clear what they are doing -- they are blatantly trying to kill him in there." "They just want to keep him in there as long as possible and hopefully just silence him," said Kasim.(With inputs from agencies)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: VVS masterclass will be knowledge sharing
articles.summary: Cricket News: Bengaluru: While the Indian cricket team made its Asian Games debut in Hangzhou in 2023, its first appearance at a multi-sport event came at the 1998 .
articles.body: Bengaluru: While the Indian cricket team made its Asian Games debut in Hangzhou in 2023, its first appearance at a multi-sport event came at the 1998 Commonwealth Games. In Kuala Lumpur, a star-studded side featuring Sachin Tendulkar, Anil Kumble, VVS Laxman and Harbhajan Singh bowed out in the league phase. Twenty-five years later, Laxman returned to the multi-sport arena, this time as coach, guiding India to gold in Hangzhou.Now, as the Shreyas Iyer-led Indian team prepares to defend its title at Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi Prefecture, Japan beginning with the quarterfinals on Sept 28, Laxman spoke exclusively to TOI of the unique appeal of multi-sport events, India's Asian Games campaign and the experience of being part of the cricket team's journey from its first CWG appearance to maiden Asian Games gold."My first experience of a multi-discipline event was at the 1998 Commonwealth Games. The whole experience of being part of the Indian contingent feels really great, and that kind of experience every young cricketer should get. It's great that I've had that opportunity both as a player and coach," said the head of cricket at the BCCI Centre of Excellence.Recalling the Hangzhou experience, the former batting great said, "Obviously, it's not like your mainstream cricket series or tournaments that we've been part of since we started playing for the country. The Asian Games was a great experience and exposure because not often do we get to visit the Games village, meet a sportsperson from other disciplines, interact with them, see how they train and prepare. A group of us went to support the Indian badminton team, which was fantastic."India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka are the seeded teams making the quarterfinals directly, with Afghanistan, Japan, Nepal, Hong Kong, Malaysia and Oman fighting for the other four knockout berths.While India will start favourites, they can ill afford to take the other teams lightly, with Nepal giving them a run for their medal in the previous edition before India won by 23 runs to make the semifinals.India will play a match against Japan and train in Tokyo for three days before heading to the host city. Laxman pointed to the match against Nepal and said, "One thing which we have learnt playing the game is never underestimate your opponent."Beyond the game, Laxman believes it is about knowledge sharing."Given the experience and the exposure the Indian cricketers have, at the end of the match it's also about sharing that experience with players from other countries. After Nepal ran us close in the previous edition of the Asian Games, their coach invited me to talk to the team, which was an opportunity to share knowledge. It's not just me, but that's the way the entire group of players will approach the experience," Laxman stated.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘How can this happen?’: Suryakumar Yadav opens up on shock India snub after T20 World Cup triumph
articles.summary: Cricket News: Suryakumar Yadav has finally opened up on the shock of losing his place in the Indian team just months after leading the side to the T20 World Cup tit.
articles.body: Suryakumar Yadav has finally opened up on the shock of losing his place in the Indian team just months after leading the side to the T20 World Cup title.The World Cup-winning captain was overlooked by the Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee for the next series against Ireland and England, with Shreyas Iyer chosen to take over the T20I captaincy.The decision brought an abrupt end to Suryakumar’s tenure despite India not losing a series under his leadership and winning both the T20 World Cup and Asia Cup during his time as captain.Suryakumar's batting form, however, had been a major concern. Runs had dried up over the previous two years and he did not register a single half-century for India in 2025. At the T20 World Cup, his only notable innings came against the USA at his home ground, the Wankhede Stadium.Speaking to former India batter Aakash Chopra on his YouTube channel, Suryakumar revealed that he initially smiled when he discovered he had been left out.“I smiled when my name was not there. Because when I played cricket with the team for a year or two, and whenever I am playing, so whenever I have been in situations like where there is pressure, where things are not going my way, I have always smiled. I have relaxed. And this is what I have seen: the moments in the past when I have had opportunities to do well. I have been grateful,” said Suryakumar.‘Even I had not thought that this would happen’The 35-year-old admitted he had expected to continue leading India beyond 2026 and believed there were more major challenges ahead, including the Olympics and another T20 World Cup.However, he said he eventually accepted that the selectors were entitled to take a different view and make the decision they believed was best for the team's future.“Obviously, the situation that has come now, even I had not thought that this would happen. After coming in 2026, I felt that, going forward, I would be taking this team forward for another two years. The Olympics will come. Then there will be another T20 World Cup, another challenge going forward. But at the same time, what you think and what the other person thinks are two different things. It is important for them to respect their own thoughts. If they thought that going forward, this is a better call, they took that call. But I didn't react. Because I felt that this was their call. They took that call in that moment. Going forward, if this team can do well under someone else, no problem,” he added.Suryakumar insisted he had no issue with Shreyas being chosen as his replacement and spoke highly of his former teammate. Yet, he admitted the decision was difficult to understand given the results India had achieved during his captaincy.“I have seen the team that they have chosen. I have also played a lot of cricket with Shreyas. And I know he is a good player, a good human being, and a good captain also. So, I was not like, ‘Why did they make him the captain?’ But yes, I was a little disappointed. Because you have not lost a single series in two years. You have won the World Cup and the Asia Cup. Then you want the same thing to go forward. Because when everything is going well, then why? What is the reason for the change? What is the reason for the change? It was going on in my mind. I was sitting at home for a month and a half,” said SKY.‘How can this happen?’Suryakumar revealed that the disappointment became harder to deal with once he was left alone to process what had happened. He said the questions over the decision continued to run through his mind after India’s World Cup triumph.“I was thinking, how can this happen? How is it possible? We just won the World Cup. Yes, IPL was not as good as how I wanted. We were sitting at home. Friends came, family came. Everyone said that it's okay. Part of life. But then, when they leave the house. We stay alone at home,” he added.The India batter also revealed that the selectors informed him about their decision shortly before the squad for the England series was officially announced.According to Suryakumar, the selection committee called him two to three days before the announcement and told him that it was time for India to move forward without him.“They called me 2-3 days before the team was announced. They called me, saying it's time to move on. I didn't react. Because it's not my fault. That's not how SKY has ever been. Whatever call someone took. He must have thought that this was better for the team. Going forward, this will be a good call. You took the call. You told me. There is no problem,” said SKY.Despite being dropped, Suryakumar made it clear that he remains available for India and will continue playing, ready to return whenever the selectors believe the time is right.“I am ready. You can call me anytime. I am playing cricket anytime. I will continue to play. Whenever you feel the time is right. Things are right,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Has to be a joke': Pakistan-born cricketer hits out at PCB amid Imran Khan row
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former Australia cricketer Usman Khawaja has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) after it complained to a British broadcaster for an interview.
articles.body: Former Australia cricketer Usman Khawaja has criticised the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) after it complained to a British broadcaster for an interview with the sons of former Pakistan Prime Minister and World Cup-winning captain Imran Khan.Khawaja, who was born in Islamabad, reacted after reports claimed the Pakistan team had threatened to boycott the second Test against England if the broadcaster aired the interview with Imran Khan's sons, Sulaiman and Kasim.The interview was eventually broadcasted, although later than originally scheduled, and Pakistan returned to the field.The PCB lodged a complaint with Sky Sports over the broadcast. Khawaja responded to a social media post about the complaint, writing: “This has got to be a joke".Imran Khan, 73, has been in jail in Rawalpindi since 2023 after being convicted on corruption charges. Earlier this week, he underwent a medical examination in Islamabad before being taken back to prison.His sons have raised concerns about his safety and alleged that attempts are being made on his life.Khawaja's former Australia teammate Pat Cummins also spoke about the issue, saying Imran's family should be allowed access to him.Cummins backed former Australia captain Greg Chappell and 20 other former international captains who recently appealed to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to ensure proper medical care and humane treatment for Imran.Cummins said he hopes the court-ordered medical assessment is completed and that family visits continue. He also called for Imran to be treated with dignity in a post on X while sharing a video of Chappell expressing concern over the former Pakistan captain's health.Cummins became one of the first active international cricketers to publicly support calls for Imran's medical care after 21 former captains, including India's Sunil Gavaskar, signed the letter to the Pakistan Prime Minister.Before entering politics, Imran Khan led Pakistan to its first and only ODI World Cup title in 1992 and remains one of the country's most recognised cricket figures.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Second division cricket’: Michael Vaughan brutally mocks Pakistan batting at Lord’s
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan’s struggles in England have deepened after their batting collapsed for 110 in the first innings of the Lord’s Test, prompting a brutal assess.
articles.body: Pakistan’s struggles in England have deepened after their batting collapsed for 110 in the first innings of the Lord’s Test, prompting a brutal assessment from former England captain Michael Vaughan.Pakistan arrived at Lord’s hoping for a response after being beaten by an innings and 53 runs in the opening Test. The return of regular captain Babar Azam had also provided some optimism, but his comeback did little to change the visitors’ fortunes.Babar managed only eight runs, while Abdullah Shafique (5), Shan Masood (1) and Mohammad Rizwan (7) all fell cheaply. Opener Azan Awais offered some resistance with 46, but Pakistan were bowled out for just 110.Vaughan was scathing in his assessment of the Pakistan batting line-up, arguing that England’s bowlers were operating without any real fear of being punished."I'll be brutally honest. The England bowlers aren't being challenged at all. And this Pakistan batting lineup is possibly the easiest batting lineup I've seen in a long time to bowl to. And not only that, I think as a bowler, I think they're all queuing up to bowl because they know there are wickets out there," Vaughan said on the BBC Test Match Special."You're not going to get hurt. There's no batter that's going to hurt them. No one's going to damage their figures, and it's really, 'roll up, roll up, who wants to get the wickets?'," he added.The former England skipper continued his criticism by questioning whether Pakistan’s current batting unit was even of Test-match standard.With England’s bowlers repeatedly finding breakthroughs, Vaughan suggested the visitors had made life remarkably easy for the hosts."I think they all know that Pakistan aren't going to get big scores. So you're only going to be out there for 40 to 50 overs, so you give everything in every spell, you keep going to Joe Root saying, Err, I'll bowl another one.' There are so many wickets out there," said Vaughan.He then made a particularly harsh comparison, suggesting Pakistan’s batting resembled a second-division county side rather than an international Test team."It's so easy. They're still doing a good job, and they're still looking very threatening. And I think this bowling attack, the way they're bowling, will challenge better batting lineups if they continue in this fashion. But this is Pakistan batting. Is it second division county cricket? There's no way that they are batting in any standard to say that, that is a Test match batting lineup," he added.Pakistan’s batting woes have been compounded by the absence of opener Imam-ul-Haq, who did not bat in the first innings after suffering a calf strain while fielding at Lord’s.England capitalised on Pakistan’s collapse to take a commanding position in the Test. The hosts finished the second day on 81/3 in their second innings, extending their overall lead to 261 runs.After Pakistan’s innings ended inside 38 overs, England remain firmly in control of the second Test and have put the visitors under immense pressure to produce a turnaround in the remainder of the match.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: My grandfather and father made me fall in love with cricket: Cheteshwar Pujara
articles.summary: Cricket News: Cheteshwar Pujara, who was one of Team India's most reliable batters in Test cricket and played a key role in Team India's first ever test series win .
articles.body: Cheteshwar Pujara, who was one of Team India's most reliable batters in Test cricket and played a key role in Team India's first ever test series win on Australian soil in 2018-19, says watching cricket matches on TV with his grandfather (Shivlal Pujara) and father (Arvind Pujara) during childhood was one of the key reasons he fell in love with the sport. Pujara, who has 19 Test centuries to his name, tells us, "My grandfather was a cricketer, and my father played the sport too. So, the love for cricket runs in our family. Back in those days, not all international matches were televised, but I would watch all televised matches involving the Indian team with my father and grandfather. I remember being glued to the TV and watching Sachin (Tendulkar) paaji in action against top sides like Australia and Pakistan in ODI cricket. It was fascinating. So, I got into the sport thanks to my grandfather and father."Pujara, who lost his mom (Reena Pujara) when he was just 17, adds, "I also owe a lot to my mother for the way she brought me up. When I was disappointed after not getting picked for the under-15 Indian team even after an unbeaten triple hundred at the under-14 level for Saurashtra, she told me that I was talented enough and will certainly make it to the Indian team one day. She always had that confidence in me, and that gave me immense self-belief. Hailing from a normal middle-class family, I owe whatever I have achieved today to the values she instilled in me early in life. While she never said ‘no’ to any of my demands, including playing video games, she made sure I never neglected my studies. She taught me time management at a very young age. The most important lesson she taught me was when she told me, 'You may not become famous or successful as a cricketer, and that is fine. But you must become a good human being first.' Those words have always stayed with me."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Javed Miandad's emotional Imran Khan plea: 'What will happen if you let him out?'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan batting great Javed Miandad broke down in tears while speaking about the imprisonment of his former teammate and captain Imran Khan, insistin.
articles.body: Pakistan batting great Javed Miandad broke down in tears while speaking about the imprisonment of his former teammate and captain Imran Khan, insisting that Khan is not corrupt and appealing for his release.Miandad, 69, played in six World Cups between 1975 and 1996 and was part of the Pakistan team that won the 1992 World Cup under Khan's captaincy.Khan, who served as Pakistan's Prime Minister from 2018 to 2022, has been in jail since 2023 after being convicted on corruption charges.Miandad's comments came after Khan underwent a medical examination in Islamabad before being taken back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. Khan's party has questioned the way the examination was conducted, pointing out that Pakistan's Supreme Court had ordered his transfer to Shifa International Hospital, where he was to have access to a team of doctors, including his personal physician.The issue around Khan's health has also been raised by his sons. On Thursday, Sulaiman and Kasim Khan spoke to former England cricketer Michael Atherton at Lord's during the second Test between England and Pakistan.They said their father's condition was deteriorating and alleged that he was being kept in isolation for nearly 23 hours a day.Speaking about his former captain's continued imprisonment, Miandad became emotional as he defended Khan's character.“He is an honest man. He is not someone who engages in corrupt practices, otherwise he would have done a lot of things. What will happen if you let him out? Will he harm someone? He is also someone’s son. I always think about what he must be doing,” Miandad said on the Narrative YouTube channel.Miandad and Khan were among the players who helped Pakistan become a force in international cricket during the 1980s and 1990s.Their partnership was key to Pakistan's 1992 World Cup campaign. In the final against England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, Pakistan were in trouble early in their innings before Khan and Miandad put together a 134-run partnership.Pakistan went on to win the match and claim their first World Cup title.Imran Khan's sons' interview sparks controversyThe issue gained further attention on Thursday after reports said the Pakistan team had threatened not to take the field following an interview given by Khan's sons to a British broadcaster.Kasim Khan accused those holding his father of deliberately prolonging his imprisonment.“It’s very, very clear what they’re doing, which is they’re just blatantly trying to kill him in there,” Khan’s son, Kasim claimed. “They just want to keep him in there as long as possible and hopefully just silence him,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Mai wicket-taker hoon': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi sends message to 'Ishan bhaiya' ahead of Duleep Trophy semifinal
articles.summary: Cricket News: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has opened up about his bowling spell in East Zone's opening Duleep Trophy 2026 match, saying he always enjoys b.
articles.body: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has opened up about his bowling spell in East Zone's opening Duleep Trophy 2026 match, saying he always enjoys bowling and joking that captain Ishan Kishan did not know he was a "wicket-taker."Sooryavanshi, who was named East Zone vice-captain for the tournament, made an impact with the ball in the second innings against North East Zone. The left-arm spinner took two wickets in a three-over spell as East Zone completed an innings and 210-run win on Tuesday.Speaking in a video shared by BCCI Domestic, Sooryavanshi said batters enjoy bowling just as much as bowlers enjoy batting."If you ask any batter, they always enjoy bowling. A batter always enjoys bowling and a bowler always enjoys batting equally," Sooryavanshi said.The teenager said Kishan brought him into the attack because East Zone needed a breakthrough, but added that the captain did not know what he was capable of with the ball."Opponent team's wickets weren't falling, so I was asked to bowl two or three overs. Ishan bhaiya felt like he was taking a risk, but he didn't knew that I am a wicket-taker," he added.Sooryavanshi's spell changed the innings quickly.He first dismissed Kishan Lyngdoh, who was caught at deep covers while trying to play an aerial shot. Three balls later, he got left-handed batter Imliwati Lemtur to edge behind, with Kishan taking the catch behind the stumps.The Bihar youngster said he knew he had only three overs to bowl and wanted to make the most of them."I had only one thing in my mind: that even if I take five wickets, I'm only going to get to bowl three overs only. So (the plan) was to bowl as well as I can and target one spot only and finish my spell well.”The Rajasthan Royals batter did not have much success with the bat in the match. He scored eight in East Zone's only innings but said contributing with the ball made up for it."It was a lot of fun because batting didn't go so well in the match. So, contributing with the ball was great. And of course, when a batter takes a wicket, there's no greater enjoyment than that, so it was a lot of fun!" he concluded.Sooryavanshi now has four wickets in First-Class cricket.East Zone have qualified for the Duleep Trophy semi-finals and will face Central Zone at the BCCI Centre of Excellence Ground 2 in Bengaluru. The match starts at 9:30am on Sunday, while the final begins on September 6.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: England vs Pakistan 2nd Test Live Score: Harry Brook, Emilio Gay look to pile on runs but rain threatens to w
articles.body: UPDATE - 10.21 am GMT - Rain eases to a drizzle as ground staff get back to work on the covers. Yet it is a bit dark, and a resumption still looks some distance away.. UPDATE - 10.10 am GMT - The drizzle has intensified into a steady downpour now, and there is no action happening on the field as well. The covers remain fully on. The waiting game continues.... Game stopped due to : Rain Stoppage. UPDATE - 9.40 am GMT - It is currently drizzling here at Lord's and the covers are on. There are also some dark clouds hovering over the ground. Let's hope it goes away and the rain stops. The start of the play is officially delayed..ENG vs PAK Live: Weather updates Play has been delayed at Lord's Cricket Ground as persistent rain and thundery showers impact the area. The current temperature stands at 17°C with a very high humidity level of 91%..ENG vs PAK Live: Imam-ul-Haq injury cost Pakistan Pakistan's problems were compounded by the absence of opener Imam-ul-Haq, who suffered a left calf strain while fielding on the opening day and has been ruled out of the remainder of the Test. The visitors' batting lacked both stability and depth, with Azan Awais' 46 the only meaningful contribution as wickets tumbled around him. Babar's return also failed to provide the boost Pakistan had hoped for. The captain was dismissed for just eight, while Abdullah Shafique and Shan Masood were among the early casualties as England's seamers exploited the conditions at Lord's..ENG vs PAK Live: Pakistan bowled out for 110 Pakistan had earlier been bowled out for just 110 in 37.2 overs, handing England a huge 180-run first-innings advantage. The collapse came despite the return of captain Babar Azam and left Pakistan with a mountain to climb after their batting order struggled against England's pace attack. Ollie Robinson was the chief destroyer, finishing with remarkable figures of four for 11 from 13 overs, including six maidens. Jofra Archer provided sustained hostility and claimed three for 26 from 11.2 overs, while Josh Tongue picked up two wickets. Gus Atkinson went wicketless despite keeping the pressure on Pakistan's batters..ENG vs PAK Live: England lose three early wickets The hosts ended Friday on 81 for three in their second innings after bad light brought play to an early close. Ben Duckett, Jordan Cox and Joe Root fell during the final session, but England remained firmly in control with a substantial lead already in the bank..ENG vs PAK Live: England seize control at Lord’s England will resume the second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s in complete command after ending Day 2 with a 261-run lead. After being bowled out for 110 in just 37.2 overs, Pakistan handed England a huge 180-run first-innings lead.. A crucial morning session - While the weather forecast predicts passing showers that might cause interruptions, the game is moving at a rapid pace and a decisive result remains well within sight. Pakistan need something truly special from their strike bowlers in this opening hour to claw their way back into contention, while England will aim to bat the opposition completely out of the game. Grab your cup of tea and settle in because another exciting day of Test cricket is about to get underway.. Hosts aiming to build a fortress - England will want to tighten up after losing three early wickets yesterday and focus on constructing steady partnerships. With tricky overhead conditions expected throughout the day, the overnight batters need to show watchful defense early on to absorb the initial burst from the Pakistani seamers. Once the lead stretches past three hundred, the English pacers will be eager to get the red ball in hand and unleash their relentless accuracy once more under helpful overcast skies.. Visitors seeking discipline and fire - For Pakistan, the primary learning from their first innings collapse is the desperate need for application and patience at the crease. Their top order cannot afford loose strokes against a high quality pace attack and must learn to leave the ball whenever needed. Before their batters get another chance, their pacers need to make the morning session count by targeting the stumps and bowling tighter lines to wrap up the English lower order before the target slips completely out of reach.. A cloudy morning at the Home of Cricket - Hello and a very warm welcome back to Lord's for moving day of this riveting Test match between England and Pakistan. The dark London clouds are hovering above, but the atmosphere inside the ground is electric. England find themselves firmly in the driver seat, holding a massive lead of 261 runs with seven wickets still in hand. With three full days left in the contest, the hosts will look to tighten their grip on the match and seal the series, while Pakistan face an uphill battle to stay in the contest.. ... DAY 3, SESSION 1 .... That's a wrap - That brings us to the end of an eventful Day 2 of this second Test, with England firmly taking the upper hand and Pakistan now facing a huge challenge to save the game. Day 3, also known as ‘Moving Day’, gets underway at 10 am GMT, but you know the drill - join us well before that for all the build-up. Cheers!. The pacers turn up the heat - Pakistan’s pacers came out firing after the break and gave England plenty to think about, with Khurram Shahzad making early inroads by removing Duckett and Cox. They were also unlucky at times, beating the edge repeatedly without the resulting chances carrying to hand. Root and Gay then steadied England with a 47-run stand before Ali got Root for 24, bringing Brook to the crease. The England batter had a huge lbw appeal to survive first ball, but settled quickly and, with Gay holding firm at the other end, the pair guided England through the rest of the session. Pakistan finally had something to cheer about with the ball, but England still hold the advantage.. Pakistan crumble - Pakistan needed a big partnership after lunch, but England simply kept the pressure on. Awais battled hard for his 46, riding his luck at times, but found precious little support as wickets continued to fall around him. Robinson was outstanding, taking four, while Archer claimed three and Tongue two as Pakistan folded for just 110, handing England a commanding 180-run lead. Imam-ul-Haq’s absence due to his calf injury made Pakistan’s task even tougher.. England finish the job - Pakistan began the day with England on 248/9, but the hosts quickly added 42 runs to stretch their total to 290, with Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue putting together a valuable last-wicket stand. Pakistan’s response was then rocked almost immediately, losing Shan Masood and Abdullah Shafique as England’s seamers found their rhythm. articles.title: Geoffrey Boycott reveals he offered to help Harry Brook reach the ‘realms of Lara and Tendulkar’ but was ignored
articles.summary: Geoffrey Boycott revealed he offered to mentor Harry Brook to help him reach the level of Sachin Tendulkar and Brian Lara, but his advice was ignored.
articles.body:
England legend Geoffrey Boycott claims Harry Brook could reach the level of Brian Lara and Sachin Tendulkar but wastes his talent.

Boycott revealed he offered advice through Brook's uncle at Headingley, but never heard back from the batter himself.

Brook hasn't scored a Test century in over a year, despite averaging 53 and holding the world's No. 1 ranking.

Geoffrey Boycott reveals how Harry Brook snubbed his mentorship

Geoffrey Boycott hasn't held back his admiration for Harry Brook's raw ability, but the Yorkshire legend has revealed a personal frustration too, as an offer to help the England batter never got a response.

Boycott, never one to hand out compliments lightly, described his fellow Yorkshireman as a player blessed with rare natural gifts, even if that talent isn't translating into consistent results.

Despite currently being ranked the world's No. 1 Test batter, Brook hasn't managed a century in the format for over a year now, a surprising drought given his overall average sits at a healthy 53.

Against Pakistan at Headingley, he looked fluent en route to 91, only to fall cheaply for just 15 in the second Test at Lord's.

However, Boycott didn't hold back when explaining just how good he thinks Brook could be.

"I've said before and I'll say again, I've seen a lot of players. I haven't seen anybody with the talent he's got for a long time. Enormous talent. The timing, the shot playing, he's tall, big reach, but his thinking is just unbelievable," he said in episode three of the Geoffrey Boycott: An Extraordinary Innings podcast.

According to Boycott, the issue isn't skill. But it's decision-making, particularly Brook's tendency to approach Test cricket with a white-ball mindset that often costs him his wicket cheaply. He went as far as suggesting Brook could sit among the game's true greats if he sharpened that side of his game.

"If he wants to carry on playing that way, he'll have a decent career, but he has the ability, if he could think better, to be in the realms of Lara and Tendulkar. And, whoa, that's a bit special," he said.

"To be up in that stratosphere is huge. There ain't many above them, except Bradman, and that's special. But he plays one-day cricket to every ball. He doesn't have a look at the ball, he has to bash the first ball. He'll just keep getting caught at mid-off and mid-on and daft places."

How did Boycott's offer of help go unanswered?

Impressed by the talent of Brook, Boycott was ready to hit the training nets with the batsman. The veteran revealed how Brook's uncle sought him out at Headingley last year to have a word with his cousin.

"His uncle came to me last year and he said, 'Would you have a word with him?' Well, he asked me what I thought of him. I told him exactly this. He said, 'Really?' I said, 'Yeah.' I said that much ability is rare, special" Boycott recalled.

He then went on to add: "He said, 'Would you have a word with him?' I said, 'It's not for me to go to him. He might tell me to, you know, off' I said. But if he asked me, of course I'd help. Why would I not? I gave him my number and never heard a word."

A fair critique, but timing and trust matter as well

Boycott's assessment of Brook's talent isn't remotely far-fetched. Very few would argue against the idea that he possesses rare ability at this level. What's more interesting is the human element buried in this story, which is an offer of mentorship that simply went nowhere, despite coming through a trusted family connection rather than an unsolicited approach.

It's worth remembering, though, that not every player responds well to unsolicited advice, even well-intentioned advice from a legend of the game. Brook may already be working through these issues with England's current coaching setup, and silence doesn't necessarily mean disrespect. It could simply reflect a player choosing to trust the voices already inside his own camp.

Still, Boycott's core point about decision-making holds weight. Talent alone rarely separates good players from all-time greats; it's shot selection under pressure that usually does. If Brook can eventually marry his natural gifts with better judgement at the crease, Boycott's lofty comparisons might find more backers.
